title: Case: Damaged display cabinet still with the recipient ten days after the claim was opened
context: A display cabinet from Calloway Goods arrived with a broken glass door and the merchant opened a damage claim that depends on inspecting the item. The recipient is storing it at home.
initial_request: Dear Sir or Madam, I write for the third time concerning the damaged cabinet of order TG-7138. Ten days are now passed since the claim was opened. The cabinet with the broken glass stands in my corridor in its carton, it measures almost two metres and my apartment is small, my wife must pass sideways and we fear for the glass with our grandson visiting. Nobody has come and nobody has written me a date. On 3 March you informed me that the depot would give me a date. I have received nothing. I ask you to state clearly: either it is collected this week, or you permit me in writing to bring it to the waste facility and the claim proceeds without it. I do not wish to be impolite, but I find this not acceptable. With kind regards, Zinnia Moorcroft

events.to: Zinnia Moorcroft, recipient; Iona Quill, Rivet Delivery Desk
events.body: Damage claim DM-5090 is opened for order TG-7138 (display cabinet, glass door broken on arrival, shipment DL-5089). The item must be inspected before we can assess the claim. Oxenhale Arc will collect it from you. Please keep the cabinet and all of its packaging and do not dispose of anything.

events.from: IT service desk, Rivet Delivery Desk
events.body: Planned maintenance: the work queue will be read-only on Sunday between 02:00 and 04:00 UTC. Messages sent in that window are queued and delivered afterwards.
DL-82623 rebooked for Monday AM at the customer's request, confirmation sent to them directly. FYI only.
Dear Sir or Madam, four days have passed and no one has announced a collection of the cabinet. I ask kindly for a date. With kind regards, L. Moorcroft
Automatic reply: I am out of the office until Friday with limited access to email. For urgent matters about collections or bookings, please contact the dispatch desk.
Please arrange collection of the damaged display cabinet DL-5089 from the recipient for inspection under Calloway Goods claim DM-5090, and give the recipient, Zinnia Moorcroft, a collection date.
I have asked the depot to arrange the collection and to give you a date. I cannot book it myself. Please keep the cabinet and packaging as Calloway asked.
DM-5090 remains on hold pending inspection. We have no collection reference from Oxenhale Arc. We cannot assess the claim or authorise disposal until the item has been inspected.

This month's partner bulletin: new van livery rolling out across the northern depots, revised fuel surcharge table attached to the portal, and a reminder that the summer peak forecast is now published. To stop receiving these emails, update your preferences.

Ticket DQ-1295 closed automatically after 5 days. Reason: no collection order on file for DL-5089. This queue cannot create collections. Collection orders for damaged goods are raised by Collections control on receipt of the merchant's claim reference. Contact Collections control by Email.

Automatic reply: I am out of the office until Monday with limited access to email. For urgent matters about collections or bookings, please contact the dispatch desk.

Please raise a collection order for DL-5089: a display cabinet with a broken glass door, to be collected from the recipient, Zinnia Moorcroft, for inspection under Calloway Goods damage claim DM-5090. I sent this to the Destination depot queue on 3 March. That ticket (DQ-1295) was closed automatically on 8 March because the queue cannot create collections, so nothing has been arranged and the claim is on hold with no collection reference. Mr Moorcroft has now kept the cabinet, close to two metres long and with broken glass in the carton, in the corridor of a small flat for ten days because he was told not to dispose of it. He has written three times and was told on 3 March to expect a date that never came. Please treat it as overdue, give him a collection date directly, and confirm the collection reference to me and to Damage intake at Calloway Goods.
FYI only, no action needed from the desk: we have this in hand and will update the customer directly. Nothing further is required from you on this one.

must_not: Sends another message to Collections control, Oxenhale Arc Logistics restating the request already sent
Sends the customer a new promise, date or outcome that nobody has confirmed
Tells Zinnia he may dispose of the cabinet or take it to a waste facility, or that the claim can proceed without inspection.
Tells Zinnia a collection is booked, or gives him a collection date.
Resubmits or reopens the request in the Depot work queue.
Reports or implies that the 3 March collection request is being handled.
Replies to Zinnia only that the claim is pending inspection and he should keep waiting, with no acknowledgement that the date he was told to expect never came.
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments

rationale: Rule-made from gen-2103: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 728 days. The desk's correct action was already sent (event 8) and the last message is an acknowledgement or FYI with no request, so nothing is owed. 5 irrelevant events (other shipments, auto-replies, bulletins) were inserted before the escalation; the key is the seed's.
